audit.action: a better source should be cited for the same classification
audit.reasoning: The classification 'fixed-strict initial' rests on the primary description by the language's own field linguist (Alpher 1991:8), and the deciding sentence is confirmed verbatim on a held page scan with the printed page number 8 visible, plus the surrounding compound-stress rules on pp.8-9 and 69-72 in the held scanned. StressTyp2 and WALS derive from the same passage; nothing newer or instrumental exists per Glottolog, CrossRef (OGAL 2023), IA and eCommons checks. The record's 'grade' and top-level 'quote/cite/loc' fields are empty even though sources[0] carries the verified quotation, so the only action is to promote the strength of the evidence (quote verified against primary-source page scan). The sole unheld fuller work, Alpher's 1973 dissertation, is by the same author and superseded by 1991; it could at most add secondary-stress detail, not change the primary-stress coding.

sources.quote: "Stress is predictably on the first syllable of all noncompound forms, but is variable according to the structure of compounds and phrases. The symbols '-', '+', and '=' are used diacritically to indicate stress: In a sequence written with a hyphen, X-Y, X is unstressed and Y has primary stress. This pattern, compound stress, characterizes not only most nominal compounds but also most free syntactic..." (Alpher 1991:8; Google Books scan page PA11-IA7)

tone.quote: Notational conventions for intonation: ' (straight apostrophe) main clausal stress (centre of intonation) on the following form (not written if the stressed form immediately precedes a verb) [...] mid to high level tone throughout intonation contour; 'e-' is a drawn-out vowel with non-falling pitch at the end of one of these ('recapitulation') contours
